newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher, awaiting payrolls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds higher, awaiting payrolls.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were higher in light late trading as the market awaited Friday's employment data and next week's Presidential election, traders said.
"It's really dead today," said one. "I think everything is on hold until tomorrow's employment numbers."
If the employment data do not jolt the market, "we will have to wait until the results of the (Presidential) election next Tuesday," he said.
Nonfarm payrolls are expected to have risen by 212,000 in the month, according to a Reuters survey.
Late Thursday, pass-throughs were 8/32 to 11/32 higher in coupons of 7.0 percent or smaller, and were up 2/32 to 8/32 in current and premium coupons.
Spreads over Treasuries mostly held steady.

Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 100-13/32 to yield 112 basis points over 10-year Treasury notes. Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were up 7/32 at 100-09/32 while Freddie Mac 30-years gained 8/32 to 100-15/32.
The 10-year note was up 13/32 to yield 6.35 percent.
